cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: New Rule Required
cards.instruction: Use every problem as justification for adding another rule, ceremony, checkpoint, or layer of oversight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody takes the next family photo until I've set a blinking rota. One closed pair of eyes spoiled the last one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't schedule a blink. Shall we just take three pictures?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may take three after we've rehearsed unscheduled blinking. I'll decide when everyone's ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That will take all afternoon. The children won't stand here that long.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're in charge of rehearsal duration. Set a limit for each child and report to me before we begin. I'll add a readiness check so your timetable doesn't rush the blinking.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 withholds next photo, A3 grants B2 three-shot option only after rehearsal, A5 appoints time control and adds readiness oversight; A authority creates each new rule.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 involuntary blink causes A3 rehearsal; B4 child endurance causes A5 per-child duration limits and another check. The rehearsal is intentionally impractical.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers multiple shots and B4 explains children limits, plausible photography solutions A proceduralizes.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 time-cost problem to add oversight of the oversight, deepening the same rule-making rather than merely saying no.

specificity.evidence: A1 failed family photo and B4 children waiting make the actual inconvenience concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 timetable rushing blinking is earned by B4 duration concern and A3 rehearsal.
